_note: Traceability for the farm monitor: every design decision of chapters 2-9 names the chapter-1 row (N1-N7) or brief line (B1-B5) it answers, and the file in this repository that holds the artefact. `design.py trace` reads the hazards from ../ch01/never_list.json, checks that every id cited exists, that every hazard is answered by at least one decision, that every critical hazard has a response on the device (chapter 4 or 5) and a bench test, and that every artefact path exists. It exits 1 on any gap.

brief.B1: measure air temperature and humidity in each greenhouse, soil moisture in the plot, the level of the irrigation tank
brief.B2: switch one fan per greenhouse and one irrigation valve, automatically within limits the farmer sets, and manually from the phone
brief.B3: live values and a week of history in an app; alert the farmer when something is wrong
brief.B4: mains at the greenhouses that cuts out several times a week; Wi-Fi covers the greenhouses; the plot is 200 m away
brief.B5: under 150 USD of hardware per greenhouse, no monthly bill that scares a smallholder

decisions.decision: sensor period 15 s, status 60 s, offline after 10 misses, ±0.5 °C, 2 h local buffer
every critical computation on the device; presence, forecast, cross-greenhouse analysis and push on the cloud; the outdoor reading shared by a local hop
path B for the greenhouse nodes (status + 10-min history + events), path C for the plot node (11-byte frame)
status overwrite, history append with min/mean/max, events append with id = dev-ts-type, settings desired/reported with a version
field table: t (°C), h (%), soil (%), tank (%) with unit and physical range in the schema; null for 'could not read', never a sentinel; schema and fw in every record; readers migrate on read
settings clamped on the device, the clamped value reported back with the version
six tasks by rate; the safety task alone calls the interlock and feeds the watchdog; comms on core 0 and never in the safety path
safe states: fan on, valve closed; pull-down on every relay pin; safe states driven before any sensor or radio is initialised
decisions.test: bench: power up with the sensor unplugged; both relays must stay in their safe state and the LCD must say why

decisions.decision: watchdog fed by the safety task only, 5 s timeout, 22 s of 30 used with boot and the first reading
decisions.test: bench: stall the safety task with a debug command; the chip must reset within 5 s and come back in the safe state

decisions.decision: events through a queue to an outbox; status dropped when stale; history and events replayed in order
heartbeat gate: a second relay in series with the valve, held by a 3 s retriggerable monostable the safety task pulses
decisions.test: bench: hold the MCU in reset with the valve commanded open; the gate relay must drop within 3 s

decisions.decision: hardware max-on timer on the valve (30 min), independent of the MCU; a shorted valve relay is detected by the tank level falling while the valve is commanded closed
decisions.test: bench: short the valve relay; the firmware must declare the fault from the level trend and the timer must drop the series relay at 30 min regardless

decisions.decision: accepted: a fan stuck off is a repair call raised by the alert path, not a hazard to people; no hardware layer
greenhouse nodes on Wi-Fi; plot node on LoRaWAN class A at SF8 through one gateway; cellular excluded by X5 and by cost
comms contract: connect in stages with timeouts, clock before TLS, full-jitter backoff capped at 300 s, outbox per stream, presence judged in the cloud
per-device custom token in NVS minted by the claim flow; owner's session is the authority; per-unit hotspot password on the label; rules confine each device to its own path with shape checks
TLS roots pinned; the token-signing key and the OTA private key live on one server; identity.py scan in CI

shape A (Firebase RTDB) on the Spark plan at the brief's size: $0 a month; the two 'you build' rows (nightly export, signed OTA) written before launch; the migration to shape B keeps the records and the comms contract
listeners on /status only; charts by indexed limitToLast query; history older than 30 days exported nightly to a bucket
up_s, rst, boots, heap_min in the status record; the fleet table's five lines; alerts on counts (offline > 5 %, any loop suspect, any unit under the heap floor)
presence = status age over 10 misses per class (600 s greenhouse, 6 000 s plot), judged in the cloud; no device-written online flag
signed manifest, eight checks, pending-valid boot with rollback; rollout one greenhouse node first with an hour's soak, then the rest; the plot node is updated by a visit (no FUOTA)
decisions.test: bench: flash an image whose sensor driver is broken; the unit must roll back to the old image within the health window with both relays in their safe state

decisions.decision: bill of materials under the brief's budget; three-year cost at the brief's size and at 10 / 1 000 devices with every price's source

hazard_tests._note: Chapter 1's field 8 (one bench test per hazard), as the acceptance list for the first unit. The N7 test is the rules scenario table of chapter 7 replayed in the emulator.
hazard_tests.N1: short the valve relay driver on; the gate or the timer must close the valve within its bound and the fault must latch
hazard_tests.N2: unplug the SHT31; after three periods both actuators must be in their safe state and the buzzer must sound
hazard_tests.N3: pull the router's power; the app must show the unit offline after 10 minutes and not before
hazard_tests.N4: power-cycle with the sensor unplugged; no relay may click before the LCD shows the safe state
hazard_tests.N5: type 99 °C into the app; the device must report the clamped value and the version
hazard_tests.N6: pull the router for 30 minutes; the history chart must have no gap after reconnection
hazard_tests.N7: replay chapter 7's fourteen scenarios in the rules emulator; device A must never write device B's path
